thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: KV prefix cache surge on prod-us-west-2. 10x write amplification to kv-cache observed starting 3251234500. Auto-scaling triggered but latency climbed. Paging on-call Grace Chen.

Grace Chen: on it. joining bridge. pulling graphs.

ops-bot: Pager: severity=high, impacted=hosted-api text generation, error-rate +5%  (502s and 429s), p95 latency increased from 220ms -> 1.4s. 

Grace Chen: quick tl;dr from metrics: continuous-batching rate jumped, prefix cache write rate exploded. We see promptkey churn correlated with template-hash mismatches from recent prompt templating rollout (product).

Arjun Patel: confirming. saw tokenizer mismatch errors in model-worker logs around 3251234512: "tokenize: unknown-token-length: expected 2 got 3". Seems template rollout added optional punctuation that changed prefix hashes.

Mateo Ruiz: linking recent rollout PR #1124 that touched prompt templates. @Grace can we roll that back?

Grace Chen: Proposed mitigations: 1) revert template rollout (prod) 2) throttle continuous-batcher (set batch.max_tokens=256 -> 64) 3) invalidate KV prefix cache entries for affected templates 4) route traffic to fallback model-variant for heavy tenants. doing in that order.

support-ops: customer-impact: at least 12 paying customers saw 5xx spikes, 3 reported timeouts for generation endpoints. CS already opened tickets.

Grace Chen: executing step 2 now: reducing batch size for continuous-batcher on prod-stable pool.

Grace Chen: command: ```
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/continuous-batcher BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=64 --record
```

ops-bot: batch config change applied to continuous-batcher (prod-stable). New instances rolling.

Arjun Patel: starting prefix cache invalidation for templates tagged "prompt-template/v2". Using targeted invalidation to avoid full cache flush.

Arjun Patel: invalidation command: ```
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/svc/kv/invalidate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_INTERNAL" \
  -d '{"prefix":"prompt-template/v2","reason":"tokenizer-mismatch-regen"}'
```

ops-bot: invalidation job queued, shards: 32, ETA ~45s.

Grace Chen: monitoring error-rate and cost. p50 restored to ~260ms after batch throttle, p95 trending down. write amplification reduced from 10x -> 2.3x.

incident-bot: NOTE: fallback routing policy engaged for tier-high customers -> model-variant: redwood-compact-1. Latency higher but stable responses.

Mateo Ruiz: rolling back prompt template rollout now (PR revert deployed to canary then prod).

Mateo Ruiz: deploy logs: "deploy revert-prompt-template v1.1.3 -> success".

Grace Chen: observed template-hash collisions drop, tokenizer mismatch errors no longer emitted. continuing to watch.

support-ops: Customer updates: initial outreach sent to affected accounts. We flagged that regen and revert are in progress.

SRE-Lead: quick check — did the cache invalidation create any thundering herd on reads?

Arjun Patel: good call. We staggered shard invalidation and added backpressure: small burst window + token-bucket limiter. No read storm observed in the first 10 minutes.

Grace Chen: current state: batch throttle active (BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=64), prompt-template rollback complete, targeted prefix invalidation done. Error rate down to +0.6% above baseline. p95 ~320ms.

ops-bot: Metrics snapshot (3251234680): error_rate: 0.6%, p50: 270ms, p95: 320ms, kv_write_rate: 2.3x baseline -> 1.1x baseline. GPU utilization normalized.

Mateo Ruiz: handoff plan: I'll take next shift to validate full stability and run canary traffic for 2 hours. @Grace please capture notes + RCA draft.

Grace Chen: will compile timeline and RCA. Immediate root cause: prompt templating change produced tokenization differences -> prefix hash shift -> continuous-batcher persisted new prefixes creating cache churn and excessive writes. Secondary cause: batching config allowed large aggregated batches -> amplified writes.

SRE-Lead: add follow-ups: 1) add template change gated tokenizer-check in CI 2) add preflight that compares prefix-hash distribution for template changes 3) automatic batch throttle recommendation when prefix-churn exceeds threshold 4) safer invalidation tooling with per-customer rate limits.

support-ops: noting customer impact: 12 accounts affected, 3 escalations, estimated MTTI (time to initial mitigation) 14 minutes, MTTD ~3 minutes.

Grace Chen: drafting postmortem now. ETA for initial postmortem draft: 3251238900.

Mateo Ruiz: handoff ack. I'll be on-call until 3251236789 and will post updates in this thread. If anything regresses ping @Mateo Ruiz and escalate to SRE-Lead.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity lowered to medium. No ongoing data loss.

Grace Chen: thanks team. rough timeline + commands saved to runbook (internal link). will include exact metrics and owner assignments in RCA. :thumbsup:

support-ops: closing loop with CS on open tickets. Will include workaround suggestions for affected customers (switch to fallback model, retry/backoff).

Mateo Ruiz: logging handoff note: continued monitoring for 2 hours, if error-rate <1% and kv_write_rate ~1x for 2 consecutive 30m windows then close incident.

SRE-Lead: also schedule a postmortem review with product and devex to tighten rollout checks.

incident-bot: incident resolved (transition to follow-up) at 3251234789.
